image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) standing on a ground covered with dry leaves and dirt. The duck features the characteristic iridescent green head, white neck ring, greyish-brown chest, and grey/white body plumage. Its orange webbed feet are visible, and the blue speculum patch on the wing is distinct. The background consists of blurred foliage and tree trunks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with a yellow-green hue typical of a mallard drake.
The eye is visible against the dark green head and appears black/dark brown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is robust and compact, consistent with a healthy adult drake. Plumage texture appears dense and layered.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard breeding plumage: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and grey/brown body patterning.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The orange legs are visible. The visible foot shows clear webbing between the toes, consistent with aquatic anatomy.
The folded wings show the correct anatomical structure, including the blue speculum patch bordered by white stripes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is short, and the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers is visible at the rear of the duck.
